h1: T3 Residence Ladprao — a budget Bangkok aparthotel that trades polish for generous space and free parking
intro: If you are searching for budget accommodation in Bangkok's Lat Phrao corridor that gives you more room than a standard hotel room at an accessible price, T3 Residence tends to surface consistently in traveller discussions. The property sits at 8 Nak Niwat Soi 20, a quiet residential lane in Lat Phrao district, about 1.3 km from Central Festival EastVille. Rooms come with private balconies — and the two-bedroom apartment configuration makes it practical for groups of three or four travelling together. The building includes free parking, a gym, and three restaurants. Rates start from approximately THB 500 per night for a Standard Room, with the two-bedroom apartment unit reaching THB 1,200 and above. Trip.com scores the property at 7.6 out of 10 across 54 verified guest reviews.

body.html: T3 Residence is not a polished boutique hotel designed to impress on Instagram. It is an older residential building that has been operating as a serviced apartment for years, and the property wears its age honestly. What keeps it in the conversation for budget travellers in Lat Phrao is a combination of room footprint, free parking, and a price point that is genuinely low for Bangkok. Nak Niwat Soi 20 is a quiet, lived-in residential lane — the kind of place where local families and office workers go about their daily routines, and a 7-Eleven convenience store is never more than a few minutes on foot. It is the real Lat Phrao neighbourhood rather than a sanitised tourist precinct, and for some travellers that is exactly the point.

Across 54 verified reviews on Trip.com, the most consistent praise is for the staff. Multiple reviewers describe the reception team as friendly and quick to help resolve issues. Room size is the second most mentioned positive: the rooms are consistently described as larger than expected for the price, particularly the two-bedroom apartment, which can comfortably accommodate three to four guests and comes with a separate lounge area. Private balconies on every room type are a notable feature at this price level — useful for an evening sit-down or drying clothes during a longer stay. The property also has a gym (basic equipment), three restaurants within the building, a bar, and conference facilities.
"Room was spacious, balcony was breezy, parking was free and right there — for the price in Bangkok I was very satisfied."

The guest feedback is not uniformly positive, and it is important to address the negatives clearly. Cleanliness is the weakest category, scoring 6.5 out of 10 on Trip.com — the lowest by a margin. Several reviews describe finding insects, a musty smell in certain rooms, and bed linen that showed signs of wear. The elevator only reaches the 4th floor, while rooms on the 5th and 6th floors require stair access — a significant inconvenience with heavy luggage. Air-conditioning in some rooms is reported to take longer than expected to cool, particularly during Bangkok's hot midday hours. Room photography on booking platforms appears more flattering than the actual condition in some cases, so reviewing guest photos before booking is worthwhile.

The location within Lat Phrao works best for guests with a car or those comfortable using Grab. Nak Niwat Soi 20 is not walkable to any BTS or MRT station, so the daily rhythm here involves app-based taxis rather than public rail. That said, Grab from this area of Lat Phrao tends to be quick and affordable. Central Festival EastVille — with a supermarket, cinema, and restaurants — is 1.3 km away. The Chokchai 4 night food strip, one of Bangkok's best-known late-night street-food corridors, is a short ride in the same direction. For travellers who are actually spending time in the eastern Lat Phrao / Bang Kapi corridor rather than commuting daily to the city centre, the location is perfectly practical.

Bottom line — T3 Residence fills a specific niche: budget accommodation in Lat Phrao that prioritises room size over hotel-standard finish. A score of 7.6 out of 10 is an honest reflection of that equation: friendly staff and generous space on one side; inconsistent cleanliness and an ageing building on the other. If you are travelling with your own car, want free parking and a room larger than a typical Bangkok hotel box, and are not expecting a renovated interior, this property represents fair value for its price bracket.

highlights.title: Spacious Rooms with Private Balconies
highlights.text: The two-bedroom apartment suits groups of 3–4 sharing; even standard rooms come with a private balcony — rare at this price in Bangkok.

highlights.title: Free Private Parking + Gym
highlights.text: On-site parking at no extra charge is one of T3 Residence's clearest advantages over nearby budget hotels. The gym and three in-building restaurants add convenience.

highlights.title: Real Lat Phrao Neighbourhood
highlights.text: Quiet residential soi with 7-Elevens, street food, and Central Festival EastVille 1.3 km away — an authentic local slice of Bangkok rather than a tourist strip.

honestSummary: T3 Residence is a budget option in Lat Phrao that trades a polished finish for generous room space, free parking, and a low nightly rate. A score of 7.6 tells an honest story: the staff are friendly and the rooms are spacious, but the building's age shows in both the décor and the cleanliness scores. Best for car-travelling groups on a tight budget — not for guests who expect hotel-standard hygiene throughout.
honestChecks: If consistent cleanliness is non-negotiable for you — the 6.5/10 cleanliness score, backed by multiple guest accounts of insects and worn linen, is a serious flag. Consider alternative Lat Phrao options with higher cleanliness ratings before committing.

If you have heavy luggage and may be allocated a room above the 4th floor — the elevator stops at floor 4, making floors 5 and 6 stair-only. Request a lower floor when booking and confirm it directly with the hotel before arrival.

If you rely entirely on public transport (BTS/MRT) — Nak Niwat Soi 20 is not within walking distance of any rail station. Budget for Grab fares every time you leave, or choose a hotel closer to MRT Phahon Yothin or a Yellow Line station instead.

tips.title: Request a room on floors 1–4
tips.body: The elevator only reaches the 4th floor. If you have large bags or have difficulty with stairs, specify a floor 4 or below when booking — confirm it directly with the hotel before arrival.

tips.title: Book parking in advance
tips.body: Free parking is available but limited. Notify the hotel of your vehicle when booking or call ahead before check-in to reserve a space.

tips.title: Explore the Chokchai 4 night food strip
tips.body: One of Bangkok's most authentic late-night street food corridors is a short Grab ride away. It runs past midnight and is the kind of local eating scene that makes staying off the tourist trail worthwhile.

tips.title: Use Grab rather than flagging street taxis
tips.body: In the Nak Niwat area, metered taxis on the street can be scarce. Grab responds quickly here and the fares are transparent — it is consistently the easier option for getting around Lat Phrao.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — T3 Residence Ladprao Bangkok

faq.q: Where is T3 Residence Ladprao located and what is nearby?
faq.a: T3 Residence is at 8 Nak Niwat 20 Alley, Lat Phrao, Bangkok 10230. Central Festival EastVille is about 1.3 km away (5-minute Grab). The Chokchai 4 night food strip is around 2 km. Central Plaza Ladprao and Union Mall near MRT Phahon Yothin are approximately 5 km.

faq.q: What is the starting price at T3 Residence and what room types are available?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately THB 500 per night for a Standard Room. The property also offers Superior Rooms, Queen Rooms, and a Two-Bedroom Apartment (suited for groups of 3–4) from around THB 1,200. Prices vary by date and platform — compare across booking sites before reserving.

faq.q: Does T3 Residence have free parking?
faq.a: Yes, there is free on-site parking, but spaces are limited. Notify the hotel about your vehicle at the time of booking or call ahead before check-in to secure a spot.

faq.q: Is T3 Residence convenient for getting around by MRT or BTS?
faq.a: Nak Niwat Soi 20 is not within walking distance of any rail station. The nearest MRT and BTS stops require a Grab or taxi ride. The property is best suited to guests arriving by car or those happy to use ride-hailing apps for every journey.

faq.q: Who is T3 Residence Ladprao best suited to?
faq.a: T3 Residence works best for budget-conscious travellers who want more floor space than a standard Bangkok hotel room — groups of friends, small families, or those doing business in the Lat Phrao and Bang Kapi area. Guests expecting pristine cleanliness or a newly renovated interior should look at higher-rated alternatives nearby.
